A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Janus-Pro-R1 and its image-editing extension. The complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, editing, semantic-evaluation, and ablation results in Tables 1–4 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including quantitative benchmarks, ablations, and qualitative demonstrations.

M1.justification: The SFT subtasks, GRPO training, rewards, iterative generation procedure, and editing adaptation remain unchanged. The corrected Task-II conditioning index aligns the formula with the procedure already described in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same training-data sources and coverage of GenEval, T2I-CompBench, DPG-Bench, and PIE-Bench. Counterfactual generation, multi-turn editing, and semantic evaluation are already present in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the generation, editing, semantic-evaluation, and reward-model comparisons. Newly added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendices B–C and Table 5 retain the same training budgets, sampling settings, generation-round limit, evaluation metrics, and sample descriptions. Corrections to illustrative prompt labels do not establish a changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The training-stage, model-scale, data-quality, subtask, reward-model, and counterfactual analyses are retained. The new Appendix D largely redisplays existing qualitative evidence rather than adding analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The unchanged standard-deviation calculation in GRPO is part of the algorithm, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the quantitative analysis charts are unchanged. Qualitative result descriptions are corrected in v1 Figure 3 versus v2 Figure 8: existing book images are relabeled 'three books', and cow-and-cup images receive the corresponding prompt. The same outputs are retained; no new generation results or performance gains are established.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 corrects the Task-II objective to condition on the image being evaluated, I^t, instead of I^(t-1). This repairs the mathematical specification; the remaining objectives and Appendix A derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about SFT–RL training, introspective generation, image editing, and improved semantic evaluation. The title change does not redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 newly extends the large-scale RL outlook to understanding and generation capabilities comparable to GPT-4o. Appendix E adds misuse discussion. Existing qualifications about limited evidence, counting weaknesses, and editing aesthetics remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Table 5 retain the implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, data processing, encoder selection, and inference settings. The project-page access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds FocusDiff and self-supervised meta-prompt learning citations, and removes Emerging Properties in Unified Multimodal Pretraining, Liquid, and Vila-U alongside shortened positioning discussion. The central comparison with earlier visual CoT approaches remains.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, updates author-role notes, adds acknowledgements, folds Discussion into Section 4.4, and moves Future Work into Appendix E. Most prose is retained, with localized shortening and new impacts paragraphs.

P2.justification: The full qualitative grids from v1 Figures 3–4 move to appendix Figures 8 and 7, while an abridged Aha grid remains as v2 Figure 3. The comparison grid has sharper images and corrected prompt labels; other figures and tables are reflowed without a wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The Task-II conditioning correction and repaired prompt-to-image labels remove concrete inconsistencies in v1. Clearer figure rendering and localized reorganization modestly improve presentation. Quantitative evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
